newsitem.title: UK: UK's Times March circulation falls 2.70 percent.
newsitem.headline: UK's Times March circulation falls 2.70 percent.

text.p: Circulation of the Times newspaper slipped 2.70 percent in March from February, but the paper's circulation for the six months from October 1996 to March 1997 rose 16.51 percent over the prior-year period, Britain's Audit Bureau of Circulation said on Friday.

Circulation of the Times -- the News Corp Ltd -owned paper which has been locked in a fierce circulation war against arch-rival the Daily Telegraph -- fell to 747,099 in March from 767,809 in February, the Audit Bureau said.
For the six months ended March 1997 average daily circulation rose to 783,260 from 672,292 in the year-ago period, the group said.

The Daily Telegraph, Britain's largest-circulating broadsheet newspaper, saw circulation edge up 1.52 percent in March to 1,136,857 from 1,119,852 in February. The paper, owned by Hollinger Inc, posted a 6.99 percent gain in circulation for the six months ended March 1997, rising to 1,117,281 from 1,044,281 in the year-earlier period, the Audit Bureau said.
